g3ela-30-1-teach-morph: [curious] Can you crack this one? Interview. Inter means between. An interview is a talk between two people. Every root on this page is one you already know. Read the word parts, and tap See if you cracked it. Then type the missing part of each word.
g3ela-30-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Liberated. Here's the sentence. The whole crowd of liberated statues surged back into the courtyard. One, read the sentence: the statues are alive again. Two, look for word parts: liber, ate, e d. Three, check it. Liberated means set free. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-30-1-teach-gram: [warmly] An editor hunts for capitals. lucy found mr. tumnus. Lucy is a name: capital L. Mr. Tumnus is a name too: capital M, capital T. Names get capitals wherever they are in a sentence. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the five words that need a capital.
g3ela-30-1-teach-spell: Three patterns in one pile! Cake: a silent e at the end. Boat: two vowels make one sound, a vowel team. Rewrite: a prefix, re, plus a base word, write. Think about the questions, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
g3ela-30-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Transfer. Find the root: trans. It means across. To transfer is to move something across to a new place. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-30-2-teach-vocab: Ever met someone truly amazing? Remarkable. The book says the Professor was a very remarkable man. Remarkable means so unusual it's worth talking about. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-30-2-teach-gram: Four rules, one sentence. the fauns scarf was red and lucy liked it. The needs a capital to start the sentence. Faun's needs an apostrophe: the scarf belongs to the faun. A comma goes before and. And Lucy is a name. Tap Check yourself. Then tap every word that is wrong.
g3ela-30-2-teach-spell: Pattern hunt! The goat ran to the lake. Goat: two vowels, one sound, a vowel team. Tap! Ran: short a, closed. No tap. Lake: silent e. Tap! Read the rule. Then tap every word in the two sentences with a silent-e, vowel-team or r-controlled syllable.
g3ela-30-2-teach-rwm: Let's try all three parts with a sentence from Chapter 16. Instead of all that deadly white the courtyard was now a blaze of colors. Part one, read like a reader. The statues are alive, and the courtyard is bright. Part two, read like a writer. Two pictures: deadly white, then a blaze of colors. Instead of flips one into the other. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: Instead of all that gray snow, the yard was now a carpet of green grass. Now it's your turn with the museum and the zoo. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-30-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Re. Port. Report! When you report, you carry the news back. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-30-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. After their fight, the two friends were blank. Sovereign? Hmm, no. Reconciled? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-30-3-teach-gram: Be the editor. the witchs sledge was fast and edmund was cold. The gets a capital. Witch's gets an apostrophe. A comma goes before and. Edmund is a name. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence in the gray box.
g3ela-30-3-teach-spell: Spell it by its syllables. Sunset. Sun: short u, a closed syllable. Set: short e, closed too. Sun, set. Read the rule. Look hard at each word, cover it, and write it. Then tap the card to check every letter.
g3ela-30-4-teach-morph: Quick question: what does trans mean? Across! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Transatlantic. It means across the Atlantic Ocean, like a ship sailing from England to America. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
g3ela-30-4-teach-vocab: Watch me use a word about the whole book. Reconciled. In the end, Edmund and his family are reconciled. One word, the whole story. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about the ending.
g3ela-30-4-teach-gram: Two passes, like an editor. the professors house was big and the children explored it. Pass one, capitals: The, and Professor, because it's his name. Pass two, apostrophes and commas: Professor's, and a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-30-4-teach-spell: Dice roll: pilot! Split it after the vowel: pi, lot. Pi is open, so the i says its name. Lot is closed. Tap Roll the dice, split the word, name its syllable types, and tap Check my answer.
